title: Entity record create/update/delete is broken in production: getOrCreateEntityTypeInstance mints an instance_id with no backing instance_projections row, so store.append always returns InstanceNotFound
discovered_during: WF03-gh439-testwiring-20260806 step q150 (ISS-0150 / GH #466) — surfaced the first time tests/integration/entity_subsystem_test.zig was ever executed
symptom:
Every entity record command — createRecord, updateRecord, deleteRecord — fails at runtime with EntityCommandError.TransactionFailed, wrapping StoreError.InstanceNotFound. The EXP-201 pure-validator tests pass (7 of 12); all 5 database-backed EXP-202 blocks fail identically.

Stack: entities.commands.createRecord -> store.append -> src/event_store/store.zig:330 `return StoreError.InstanceNotFound`.
root_cause:
src/entities/commands.zig `getOrCreateEntityTypeInstance()` (line ~299) INSERTs into `<tenant_schema>.entity_type_instances` and returns the freshly generated `instance_id`. Nothing anywhere in the entity subsystem then creates the corresponding row in `<tenant_schema>.instance_projections`.

`store.append()` (src/event_store/store.zig:315-330) begins by validating the instance exists:

    SELECT status FROM instance_projections WHERE instance_id = $1

and returns `StoreError.InstanceNotFound` when that returns zero rows — which it always does for an entity-type instance, because only src/engine/instance.zig:625 ever INSERTs into instance_projections, and that is the process-engine path, never reached for entity records.

Grep confirms the asymmetry: `INSERT INTO instance_projections` appears exactly once in src/ (src/engine/instance.zig:625) and `instance_projections` appears zero times anywhere under src/entities/.
reproduction:
Requires BPM_TEST_DB_URL pointing at a real PostgreSQL.

  zig build test-integration-exp

-> 7 pass, 5 fail (12 total). Each of the 5 failures is StoreError.InstanceNotFound raised from src/event_store/store.zig:330 via entities.commands.createRecord.

Direct DB confirmation that no projection row is ever produced:

  psql $BPM_TEST_DB_URL -c "SELECT count(*) FROM tenant_default.instance_projections"   -> 0

while entity_type_instances does receive its row from getOrCreateEntityTypeInstance.
impact:
EXP-202 (entity record create/update/delete via the event-sourced command path) does not work at all against a real database. The requirement is marked as covered by tests/integration/exp201_202_entities_test.zig, whose EXP-202 blocks are subject to the same defect.

This went undetected because BOTH integration files that exercise the path were effectively unexecuted: entity_subsystem_test.zig was built but attached to no build step and had not compiled since the TestHarness API changed (ISS-0150 / GH #466), and its sibling runs only inside the main_test.zig aggregate binary. The defect is in production source, not in the tests — the tests are what finally revealed it.
candidate_resolution:
Decide the intended ownership model for entity-type instances, then make it explicit:

(a) Have `getOrCreateEntityTypeInstance()` also INSERT the matching `instance_projections` row (status 'ACTIVE', a synthetic/sentinel `definition_id` for entity-type streams, `last_event_seq` 0) inside the same transaction, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING so it stays idempotent; or

(b) Give `store.append()` an explicit mode for entity-type streams that skips the instance-existence precondition, if entity records are deliberately not process instances.

(a) is the smaller change and keeps store.append's invariant intact. Whichever is chosen, the 5 currently-failing blocks in tests/integration/entity_subsystem_test.zig must go green without weakening their assertions — they assert projection row presence, version_seq progression 1 -> 2, idempotent replay returning the first record, and soft-delete stamping deleted_at.

Do NOT resolve this by relaxing the tests: the assertions describe the behaviour EXP-202 specifies.
notes:
Filed as its own issue rather than fixed inline under ISS-0150, per the WF03-gh439 handoff constraint: ISS-0150's scope is 'these tests do not actually test anything', and it is now discharged — entity_subsystem_test.zig compiles, is attached to test_integration_others_step, and executes with real assertions. What those assertions revealed is a distinct production defect in the entity command path with its own diagnose/design/fix cycle, and it is a BLOCKER-severity behaviour gap rather than a test-wiring gap.

The 5 failing blocks are left FAILING on purpose. Marking them skipped or deleting them to reach a green step would be precisely the 'never satisfy a gate by editing what it measures' anti-pattern that ISS-0150 exists to remove.
resolution: Candidate resolution (a). Added ensureEntityInstanceProjection() to src/entities/commands.zig and call it from getOrCreateEntityTypeInstance() immediately after the entity_type_instances mapping row is written, so both rows that constitute a synthetic entity-type instance are always created together. The projection row is written exactly as src/engine/instance.zig writes one for a process instance - status ACTIVE, variables {}, current_nodes [], tenant_id from bpm_effective_tenant_id() so forced RLS admits it - differing only in a NULL correlation_key and the new sentinel ENTITY_STREAM_DEFINITION_ID = 00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000e2117 for definition_id (instance_projections.definition_id is NOT NULL but carries no FK to process_definitions, so a sentinel is valid and makes entity streams identifiable without a new column). ON CONFLICT (instance_id) DO NOTHING keeps it idempotent across repeated calls and lazily self-repairs a mapping row created before this fix. All values bound as $N; only the schema name (derived from the tenant UUID by schemaNameForTenant, never user input) is interpolated. getOrCreateEntityTypeInstance additionally now takes std.mem.Allocator rather than reaching for std.heap.page_allocator internally, per the CLAUDE.md allocator rule. Data repair: migrations/1137_iss0156_entity_instance_projection_backfill.sql backfills instance_projections for every orphaned entity_type_instances row in every tenant_* schema, taking started_at/updated_at from the mapping row's created_at. Non-destructive (INSERT ... SELECT with NOT EXISTS guard + ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), skips schemas without migration 094's tables. Applied to bpm_dev and bpm_test; re-running the body reports 0 rows created. Neither database held orphans in practice (the feature never worked, so none accumulated), but a deployed database that ran the broken code would, and the code fix alone repairs those only on the next command per entity type.
verification: zig build test-integration-exp: 7/12 -> 10/12. All five StoreError.InstanceNotFound failures are gone. Create/Update/Delete entity record blocks pass fully. The two blocks still failing now fail past the root cause on their real assertions, from two independent defects filed as ISS-0159 (GH #480, idempotency duplicate branch uses the wrong record_id and leaks the AppendResult) and ISS-0160 (GH #481, record payload validation is an unimplemented TODO). Mutation check: replacing the ensureEntityInstanceProjection call with a no-op reverts exactly to 7/12 with 5x InstanceNotFound; restoring it returns to 10/12 - the fix is load-bearing. Direct DB evidence: SELECT count(*) FROM tenant_default.instance_projections WHERE definition_id = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000e2117' returns 1, where the issue's own reproduction recorded 0 rows for all entity streams. zig build exit 0 with no 'error set' output; zig build test exit 0; lint_sql_param_types 0/0/0; lint_test_wiring PASS. No test assertion was weakened and no error.SkipZigTest was added.
prevention:
The defect was a split invariant: store.append() requires an instance_projections row for any instance_id it is given, but that requirement lived only inside store.append() and was satisfied by exactly one writer (src/engine/instance.zig). A second subsystem minted instance_ids through an entirely different path and had no way to know the invariant existed. Three concrete guards:
1. instance_projections is now the single documented home of the invariant: any code that mints an instance_id must create the projection row in the same operation. getOrCreateEntityTypeInstance carries a doc comment stating this and naming store.append as the enforcer, so the next reader of the entity path sees the coupling.
2. Entity-type streams are now self-identifying via ENTITY_STREAM_DEFINITION_ID, making 'which instances are entity streams' a one-line query - an orphan-detection check (mapping rows with no projection row) is trivial to write and would have caught this.
3. The real prevention is the ISS-0150 fix that surfaced this at all: the defect survived because BOTH integration files covering the path were unexecuted - entity_subsystem_test.zig was attached to no build step and had not compiled since the TestHarness API changed. lint_test_wiring.py now enforces that every test-bearing file is reachable from a build step, which is what turned an invisible production BLOCKER into a failing test. A database FK from entity_type_instances.instance_id to instance_projections(instance_id) - which src/design/entities.md already specifies as 'REFERENCES instances(id)' but which was never created - would make this class of orphan impossible at the schema level and is worth adding when the entity subsystem is next revisited.
